defects_found.description: F28 rule (c)'s harness_version staleness check is a WHOLE-FILE content hash — a comment-only or prose-only edit to a governing file trips it exactly like a real behavior change. This wave's own edits (a one-line CONVENTION.md pointer added to MINT-RUNBOOK.md's header and to screen-worklist.mjs's header, neither changing classification/validation behavior) moved mint's and screen's harness_version and required a PENDING-RUN.md marker for each — real, measurable staleness-marker churn from a non-behavioral edit.
defects_found.root_cause: deliberate design choice, not an F28 bug: CONVENTION.md's own harness_version table (Wave MH-1) states 'any edit to any hashed file changes it... lets a proposer lane tell the harness changed apart from the input changed without reading a diff.' F28's own header explicitly considered narrowing this (diffing only non-comment lines) and rejected it — see F28-harness-run-integrity.mjs's 'CONSIDERED AND NOT NARROWED' section.

defects_found.description: Emission-in-the-harness (plan §2: 'the artifact write is part of each harness's own execution path... forgetting is not possible because there is nothing to remember') landed as CODE for screen only. For mint and fetch-drain it landed as PROSE (a mandatory runbook step; a protocol doc) — a human or lane can still skip the step, which is exactly the failure mode plan §2 says emission-in-the-harness is meant to make impossible.
defects_found.root_cause: mint has no single canonical script the way screen-worklist.mjs is — its batch procedure is a human/agent-run MINT-RUNBOOK.md sequence across several scripts and manual steps; fetch-drain's governing file (capture-worker/index.ts) is a deployed Deno edge function this repo does not import or execute as part of any local script, so there is no local 'end of main()' to wire a writeRunArtifact call into the way screen-worklist.mjs has one.
